summary: The Storage section states one concrete design fact: transfers live in a month-partitioned transfers table with a covering index on account_id. The rest is boilerplate repeated many times: structured logging with request ids, 90-day secret rotation via the vault, health/readiness endpoints, alerts paging after five minutes, schema review for index impact, sub-200 ms p95 read latency, single YAML config, low-priority backfills, unit test coverage, dashboards, and a three-phase zero-downtime migration.

claims.text: Transfers table is partitioned by month with a covering index on account_id.
Read latency target is under 200 ms at the 95th percentile.
Secrets rotate every ninety days through the platform vault.
Alerts route to the payments channel and page after five minutes.
The migration ran in three phases over two weekends without downtime.
Configuration lives in a single YAML file loaded at startup.

risks.note: 200 ms p95 target, 90-day rotation, and five-minute paging stated without source or measurement.
Migration claimed complete without downtime; no dates, metrics, or evidence given.
Section is mostly duplicated filler sentences unrelated to storage; likely padding, little reviewable content.

least_confident: Whether the covering index on account_id is meant per partition or global, since the chunk gives no schema detail.
